Locality turns the knowledge in Notion, Slack, Google Docs, Linear, and other work apps into a private, live-synced filesystem workspace for you and your AI agents.

Your company's knowledge already exists. It lives across documents, messages, issues, meetings, and calendars. But every app exposes that knowledge through a different interface, and every agent integration adds another API, tool schema, authentication flow, and runtime dependency.

Because all my data is local, I can point Codex at my Locality directory and ask it to analyze my recent meetings, draft emails, update a standup in Notion and use information from Linear and Slack for a task. The agent can use rg, write bash scripts and edit files instead of making a series of app-specific tool calls. Owning my data helps me create my own custom workflows and scripts easily across apps with just prompts.

Recently whilst tinkering with a particularly tricky project, I came across Git’s worktree feature. A tool that lets you work on multiple branches simultaneously, each in its own directory, all sharing the same underlying repository history.

All the directories above share the same commit history and are linked to the same .git object database even though each has its own working directory state.

Each directory behaves like a normal checkout, you edit files, commit and push as usual, but you avoid constantly hopping branches in a single working tree.

linked_context.page_description: Tech adoption is a social phenomenon, and AI is no different.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Even in the pre-LLM days, studies found that developer tool adoption is social. A 2011 paper 1 by Murphy-Hill and Murphy reported that developers considered watching their peers use tools to be one of the best ways to discover new tools. This is understandable given that there are countless tools out there and it takes considerable effort to try each one.

In fact, I can probably blame someone for every single piece of software that I have ever used...

The seminal book Diffusion of Innovations 2 explains that innovations spread through social interactions rather than each person evaluating the utility in isolation. Mass communication can raise awareness, but seeing someone you trust use a tool successfully is much more effective at convincing you to try it.

linked_context.page_excerpt:
Recently whilst tinkering with a particularly tricky project, I came across Git’s worktree feature. A tool that lets you work on multiple branches simultaneously, each in its own directory, all sharing the same underlying repository history.

All the directories above share the same commit history and are linked to the same .git object database even though each has its own working directory state.

Each directory behaves like a normal checkout, you edit files, commit and push as usual, but you avoid constantly hopping branches in a single working tree.

top_trends.title: You probably use AI because your colleagues use AI
top_trends.author: azhenley
top_trends.summary: Tech adoption is a social phenomenon, and AI is no different.

linked_context.page_title: You probably use AI because your colleagues use AI
linked_context.page_description: Tech adoption is a social phenomenon, and AI is no different.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Even in the pre-LLM days, studies found that developer tool adoption is social. A 2011 paper 1 by Murphy-Hill and Murphy reported that developers considered watching their peers use tools to be one of the best ways to discover new tools. This is understandable given that there are countless tools out there and it takes considerable effort to try each one.

In fact, I can probably blame someone for every single piece of software that I have ever used...

The seminal book Diffusion of Innovations 2 explains that innovations spread through social interactions rather than each person evaluating the utility in isolation. Mass communication can raise awareness, but seeing someone you trust use a tool successfully is much more effective at convincing you to try it.

source_briefs.item_name: Show HN: Locality – Sync engine to mount apps like Notion, Gmail as a filesystem
source_briefs.content_summary: Locality 是一个同步引擎，能够将 Notion、Gmail、Slack、Linear 等应用的内容作为本地文件系统挂载并保持同步。这使得 AI 编码代理（如 Codex）可以像操作代码库一样，使用 grep、bash 脚本等工具直接读取、分析和编辑这些应用中的数据，从而构建跨应用的自动化工作流。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 该项目巧妙地通过文件系统抽象层统一了各类 SaaS 应用的数据访问，极大降低了 AI 代理与外部知识源集成的复杂度，是 AI 代理基础设施领域的一个创新。

source_briefs.content_summary: 一位软件工程师提问，关于如何围绕 Python、后端系统、开源项目等技术内容建立受众。他感到虽然公开写作和构建项目，但缺乏有效的分发渠道，内容如同投入虚空。他询问哪些平台（如 X、LinkedIn、YouTube）真正有效，以及如果从今天开始该怎么做。该帖子目前显示为“[dead]”状态。

source_briefs.item_name: Barrasso: Monday will be ‘D-Day for the economy in Iran’ - The Hill
source_briefs.content_summary: 美国参议员巴拉索称，周一将是伊朗经济的“D-Day”（决战日）。美国财政部长预计将宣布对伊朗的新制裁，而德黑兰方面则驳斥了经济战的威胁。相关报道指出，美国正计划对伊朗进行经济挤压，伊朗军方领导人誓言不会屈服。

source_briefs.ai_comment: 美加贸易关系紧张加剧，高额关税和反制措施可能扰乱北美供应链，并对两国经济产生直接负面影响，是值得关注的国际贸易摩擦案例。
